text:
jamie: Quick sync — I'm putting together a canary visibility panel that joins runtime KPIs (latency, tokens, errors) with infra signals (GPU util, host queuing, pod restarts). Need to lock down metric names, tags, and ownership for each signal. Thoughts? cc @vishal @mia @ian :eyes:

vishal: Agreed. Top-level signals to show: p50/p95 latency per-route, request_error_rate (5m), tokens_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate. Infra: gpu_util_percent, host_load1, request_queue_depth, pod_restarts. Need model and route labels on runtime metrics.

mia: Can we add `rollout_id` and `variant` tags to runtime metrics? Without rollout_id it's hard to join data across the orchestration layer. Also want slices by `customer_tier` and `region`.

ian: Ops concern — adding rollout_id everywhere will blow metric cardinality in prometheus. Suggest only add rollout_id to a small set of summary counters (requests_total, errors_total, latency_histogram) and emit a separate `rollout_event` metric from the control plane that maps rollout_id -> time window.

kate: From product/UX: dashboard should include a diff panel with relative delta + direction, and a simple regression flag (pass/warn/fail). Also show sample size / confidence so PMs don't overreact to noisy signals.

jamie: Ack. Proposal: (a) runtime metrics keep model, route, variant; (b) only summary counters get `rollout_id`; (c) control plane emits `rollout_event{rollout_id,phase}` with start/end/phase labels. Does this align?

vishal: Yes. Prometheus names we should standardize on: `redwood_runtime_requests_total`, `redwood_runtime_errors_total`, `redwood_runtime_latency_seconds_bucket`, `redwood_runtime_tokens_total`, and infra `redwood_infra_gpu_usage_percent`, `redwood_infra_host_load1`. Add exemplars to link requests to traces where possible.

mia: Exemplars + traces = huge. For dashboard defaults: compare baseline vs candidate over last 30m and include traffic-weighted delta and raw counts. Also add a small cost panel: token delta * cost_per_token.

ian: I'll own infra signals and the cardinality rules. Plan: add rollout_id only to summaries, expose `rollout_event` via control-plane, and add a relabel rule to drop high-cardinality labels before long-term retention. I'll estimate cardinality impact in a doc.

observability-bot: Created ticket https://redwood.atlassian/browse/PLAT-4823 — "Canary visibility: metric schema + dashboard wireframe" (assignees: vishal, ian) :white_check_mark:

vishal: I'll draft the dashboard layout and a mapping table (metric -> query -> owner). Example queries to seed the panels: `sum(rate(redwood_runtime_requests_total{rollout_id="$rollout"}[5m])) by (variant)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_latency_seconds_bucket{route="$route"}[5m])) by (le,variant))`

mia: Also propose alerting thresholds: if candidate p95 > baseline p95 by 20% for 10m AND error_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points then mark regression. Need lookback and retry window to avoid flakiness.

jamie: Action items: vishal — dashboard + metric->query mapping by EOD Thu, ian — rollout_event + infra label constraints by Mon, mia — regression thresholds + UX flags, jamie — coordinate rollout_id tagging PR. Anyone else to add? :+1:

kate: I'll review UX flows and add guidance on how to show 'confidence' (small sample disclaimer) and the CTA for rollback/cancel.

ian: Okay — I'll post a short doc with label cardinality estimates and a helm relabel snippet.

jamie: Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge the naming table and open the PR to add rollout_event next week.

kate: :thumbsup:
